chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Oakland: recording with Billie Holiday and Vernon Alley; Marshall Royal's navy band
summary: Stationed in Oakland around 1945, he recorded with Billie Holiday at the Fairmont, and played with Vernon Alley and Marshall Royal's navy band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What did you do in Oakland?
(Inaudible)

Well, in Oakland all the musicians came through, and I got a chance to play all the clubs. As a matter of fact I recorded with Billie Holiday there, and she was at the Fairmont, I believe, or we recorded at the Fairmont. That was when she was married to Joe Guy. And Vernon Alley and I recorded with her, at the studio, the Fairmont.
What year are we talking about now?

We're talking about 1945, '44 or '45. Yes. But I was still in the army, and Vernon was in the navy, and I would go over to St. Mary's where Vernon was. You know who had the band, Marshall Royal. Tremendous band.
Was that a service band?
That was a service band, yes. I would
go over ---
Which service was Marshall in?
(Inaudible).
He was in the navy. It was a navy band.

Well, it was Marshall's band. Vernon was in the band, Buddy Collette was in the band, oh, he had a tremendous band. I think Ernie Royal was in the band, oh, they had --
Navy bands were
(Inaudible) better than the army band?
Well, I don't know. No, not really. This one -- this was a very good band. But I was in a pretty good band myself. We had Benny Green, and this --
What --

This was in Oakland. Yeah, with Benny Green and the trumpet player now who's with Sammy Davis. What's his name? Ricardo -- Rick Ricardo. We called him Flip. But any way we had a very good band, very good band ourselves. But I would play with the navy band also, and Vernon Alley and I would play civilian jobs. But any way being there was just nice because I got a chance to see everybody. And in Oakland at that time. Well, this was during the war.
